passages.original: Κατὰ στίχον μὲν ὅσα ὑπὸ τοῦ αὐτοῦ μέτρου καταμετρεῖται, ὡς τὰ Ὁμήρου καὶ τῶν ἐποποιῶν ἔπη· καταχρηστικῶς δὲ κἂν ὑπὸ κώλου ἢ κόμματος, ὡς τὸ Καλλιμάχειον τοῦτο ποιημάτιον (118) ἡ παῖς ἡ κατάκλειστος, τὴν οἵ φασι τεκόντες. καταμετρεῖται γὰρ ὑπὸ κόμματος ἀντισπαστικοῦ, καλουμένου Φερεκρατείου.
passages.english: [Poems are composed] "by the line" (*kata stichon*) when they are measured out by the same meter [throughout], as are the epic verses of Homer and of the epic poets. By an extended use [of the term, a poem is also said to be composed by the line] even if [it is measured] by a colon or a comma, as with this little poem of Callimachus (118): "the girl, the one shut away, whom they say her parents..." For it is measured by an antispastic comma, called the Pherecratean.
passages.notes: *Kata stichon*, 'by the line', means stichic composition, the same unit repeated throughout. *Kōlon* (colon) and *komma* (comma) are metrical terms for units shorter than a full line. The quoted Callimachus fragment is incomplete as cited, so its sense breaks off. The number (118) is the edition's reference number.
